title: fix(plugin-detail): the summary chip takes the percent CONVENTION, not just the scaling
body:
Fixes #9167

`percentDisplayValue` in `@object-ui/core` states the rule in its own doc comment, and the sentence is the judgement:

> If a third surface ever needs percent display, it takes BOTH halves from here — the scaling AND the convention — or this promise breaks again in the same place.

objectui#9071 moved the `summaryFields` chip onto the SCALING and deliberately stopped, because its acceptance made "any value that renders correctly today would render differently" a stop condition. So the chip went on appending a bare percent sign to the full JavaScript number, while the list cell (`formatPercent` through `PercentCellRenderer`) rounded to the field's declared precision — `0` by default — and rendered through the locale's own percent affix. One stored value, one field, two readings.

## The change

`packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx`, the chip's percent branch:

```ts
const percentField = { ...(objField as any), ...(sectionField as any) };
const precision = percentField.precision ?? 0;
display = formatPercent(num, precision, displayLocale);
const points = summaryChipPercentPoints(num);
percentValue = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, points));
```

- `formatPercent` is the list cell's own call, and it applies `percentDisplayValue` itself — so this is not a second entry into the scaling, it is the one doorway that carries BOTH halves.
- `precision` is resolved view-over-object, the same spelling the currency branch two cases above already uses, and floored at the cell's own `field.precision ?? 0`.
- `displayLocale` is a new `useDisplayLocale()` at the top of the component, never a literal `undefined` — `undefined` means the MACHINE's locale, which that hook documents as the one thing a caller must not do.
- ⛔ Nothing rounds or appends a sign locally. That is the shape objectui#9071 deleted and the doc comment names as how the promise breaks.
- The BAR still reads `summaryChipPercentPoints`, unrounded, because the list cell's own bar reads its `barValue` before formatting. Rounding the fill would make the chip disagree with the cell it just started agreeing with.

## ⭐ THE VALUE-BY-VALUE TABLE — the card's actual deliverable

Both surfaces driven in the SAME vitest run, on the SAME field (`{ name: 'ratio', type: 'percent' }`, no declared precision), from the SAME stored value, under an explicit session locale. ⛔ Not read off the call graph.

⚠️ `NBSP` below is written as a word on purpose: the affix several locales use is a no-break space, and a table written to show it is worth nothing if GitHub eats it or a reviewer cannot see it.

**Values that MOVE — every one of them onto the reading the list cell was already giving:**

| stored | locale | chip BEFORE | chip AFTER | list cell (unchanged) | agree after? | why it moved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0.123` | `en` | `12.3%` | `12%` | `12%` | yes | precision, the field default 0 |
| `12.3` | `en` | `12.3%` | `12%` | `12%` | yes | precision |
| `1.5` | `en` | `1.5%` | `2%` | `2%` | yes | precision, half-expand |
| `1.005` | `en` | `1.005%` | `1%` | `1%` | yes | precision |
| `1234.5` | `en` | `1234.5%` | `1,235%` | `1,235%` | yes | precision AND grouping |
| `0.25` | `de-DE` | `25%` | `25`NBSP`%` | `25`NBSP`%` | yes | the locale's own affix |
| `1234.5` | `de-DE` | `1234.5%` | `1.235`NBSP`%` | `1.235`NBSP`%` | yes | affix, grouping and decimal marks |
| `0.25` | `tr-TR` | `25%` | `%25` | `%25` | yes | the sign moves to the FRONT |

**Values that do NOT move — the live controls, green on both legs:**

| stored | locale | chip before and after | list cell | agree? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0.25` | `en` | `25%` | `25%` | yes |
| `0` | `en` | `0%` | `0%` | yes |
| `1` | `en` | `1%` | `1%` | yes |
| `250` | `en` | `250%` | `250%` | yes |
| `-5` | `en` | `-5%` | `-5%` | yes |
| `0.07` | `en` | `7%` | `7%` | yes |
| `-1` | `en` | `-1%` | `-1%` | yes |
| `0.5` | `en` | `50%` | `50%` | yes |

**A field that DECLARES `precision: 2`** — the authority the chip had never read at all:

| stored | chip before | chip after | list cell | agree after? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0.25` | `25%` | `25.00%` | `25.00%` | yes |
| `12.3` | `12.3%` | `12.30%` | `12.30%` | yes |
| `1234.5` | `1234.5%` | `1,234.50%` | `1,234.50%` | yes |
| `1.005` | `1.005%` | `1.01%` | `1.01%` | yes |

**Every row that moved is TOWARD the declared convention**, in the sense the card demands and not merely "different": the AFTER column and the list-cell column are byte-equal in every row, including the raw no-break space, which is asserted uncollapsed in the pin. The magnitudes were already equal before this change and still are.

### The one measured row where the two surfaces still disagree, and why it is not this card's

Same run, a field named `progress` (the cell's `WHOLE_PERCENT_FIELD_PATTERN`):

| stored | chip before | chip after | list cell | agree? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0.5` | `50%` | `50%` | `1%` | **NO — before AND after** |
| `12.3` | `12.3%` | `12%` | `12%` | no before, **yes after** |
| `57` | `57%` | `57%` | `57%` | yes |

This is a SCALING disagreement in `packages/fields`, older than this card and untouched by it: the chip's answer for `0.5` is byte-identical before and after. This change repairs one of the three rows and leaves the other exactly where it found it. Filed separately as objectui#9452 — ⛔ not folded in, because `packages/fields` is outside this card's declared file surface and adjacent to the deferred objectui#9295.

## The existing pins — moved, never routed around, never deleted

⚠️ **Surface correction.** The dispatch named two pins that would move. The disk had **four**, and the two extra were found by running the whole `packages/plugin-detail/` suite rather than by reading the call graph. The dispatch also named `summaryChipRenderers.ts` as "the chip"; on disk that file is the badge-fit set for cell-renderer routing and holds no percent logic. The percent helper is `summaryChipPercent.ts` and the branch itself is in `DetailView.tsx`. Following the disk, as instructed.

| pin | asserted BEFORE | asserts NOW |
|---|---|---|
| `summaryChip.percentSource-9071.test.tsx` | its four scaling rows agree in both places; its last case pinned the residue — the chip says `12.3%` where the cell says `12%` | the four rows are **unchanged and still green**; the last case now asserts the two agree on the SPELLING as well as the magnitude, and says which card closed it |
| `summaryChip.percentOneRule-8728.test.tsx` | eight rows of chip text; the relation "the bar draws the number the text states, clamped" as an exact equality | three rows' text moved (`12.3%`→`12%` twice, `1.5%`→`2%`); every row now also pins its **bar**; the relation is restated modulo the declared rounding, and still fails by 12.177 on the defect the file exists for |
| `summaryChip.objectValue-8464.test.tsx` (**not in the dispatch**) | subject is ROUTING — a percent keeps the chip's own text path and its own single two-span bar. Pinned `12.3%` and `Ratio: 12.3%` | same span count, same routing; the two pinned strings move to `12%` and `Ratio: 12%` |
| `summaryChip.fieldLabel-8729.test.tsx` (**not in the dispatch**) | subject is the NAME half; the relation is asserted against `textOf(chip)`, not a literal. Pinned `12.3%` and `Win Ratio: 12.3%` | relation untouched; the two pinned strings move to `12%` and `Win Ratio: 12%` |

Also updated: `packages/plugin-detail/README.md`, whose `summaryFields` section describes the chip's formatting families and said `percent` formats itself. Per AGENTS.md rule 9 (a verified claim points at the instrument that re-derives it, never at a copied figure) the new paragraph points at the pin that re-derives the table rather than copying the table into prose.

New: `summaryChip.percentConvention-9167.test.tsx`, 21 cases — the table above, executable. It pins each moved row's PRE-card spelling as a negative as well, so a revert is red here rather than merely different.

## Ablation — prediction written before the run

**Predicted:** reverting only the chip's text line (`display = formatPercent(...)` back to the bare-percent append) turns the new pin RED on all 8 moved rows, its affix case, its 4 declared-precision cases and its whole-table relation — 14 failures — while all 5 unmoved rows and the bar case stay GREEN as the lit control; objectui#8728 loses 3 rows plus its relation; objectui#9071 loses its flipped closure.

**Outcome — red, as predicted, with two corrections:**

- `Tests 19 failed | 19 passed (38)` across the three files.
- The new pin failed **15**, not 14: the accessible-name case also pins a moved row, which the prediction missed. The pin is one case stronger than predicted.
- The lit controls held: all 5 unmoved rows and the bar case stayed green, so the 19 zeros are a reading and not a void one.
- objectui#8728 lost its 3 rows but **not** its relation, and the prediction was wrong there while the pin was right: the ablation restores the pre-9167 state, in which the chip's two halves agreed exactly. That relation is about the chip against ITSELF and is objectui#8728's defect, which this ablation does not reintroduce.
- objectui#9071 lost exactly its 1 flipped case.

**Mutation proved on disk, not by an editor exit code:** anchor grep counts went `fixLine=1 bareLine=0` to `fixLine=0 bareLine=1`, and the blob hash moved `17d8be81…` to `8c8660a1…`. **Restore proved by state, not by re-running the test:** `git diff HEAD` empty AND the restored blob hash back at `17d8be81…`, identical to `HEAD`'s. The script carried a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with an absolute repo-root path throughout.

## Clause-② — declared: **no**, and the diff bears it out

The seat predicted `no`. The diff confirms it: nothing published widens. No export is added, removed or retyped; `formatPercent` and `useDisplayLocale` were already public API of `@object-ui/fields` / `@object-ui/i18n` and both packages were already imported by this exact file. `percentDisplayValue` and `formatPercent` are untouched — the contract is the thing being conformed to, not edited. This is conformance to an already-declared contract. ⛔ No `needs:contract-review`.

## Verification

All figures below are from the final commit on this branch, `c1f47c6`, except the one full-suite run named as `09b2c2a` — the only commit between them adds a `.md` paragraph and nothing else, and the gates that could move on it were re-run at `c1f47c6`.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/` — **177 files, 1653 tests**, run under the shared verify lock (`ACQUIRED after 502s`, held 257s) at `09b2c2a`'s tree. That run was what FOUND the two extra pins, so it reported them red; both were then updated and the six `summaryChip.*` files re-run at `c1f47c6` give `Test Files 6 passed (6) · Tests 73 passed (73)`. ⚠️ Stated precisely rather than rounded up: the 1653-test figure is the package suite at the moment it was measured, not a claim that the whole package was re-run after the last commit.
- `turbo run type-check --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail` — `13 successful, 13 total`, which pulled the dependency-closure builds with it. Re-run at `c1f47c6`: same verdict.
- `eslint .` inside `packages/plugin-detail` — **0 errors**, 234 files selected by eslint's own config, 1015 pre-existing warnings of classes the repo already carries. `.github/workflows/lint.yml` sets no max-warnings.
- `check:control-bytes` OK (7625 files) · `check:changeset-presence` OK · `check:changeset-claims` OK · `check:test-path-roots` OK · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` OK · `check:new-line-citations` 0 new citations.
- `check:eager-closure` — **NOT MEASURED**, not green: it answered "No eager-closure report at apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json", a missing prerequisite. This change adds no module edge (both new imports come from packages this file already imported).
- `check:doc-fences` OK (227 documents) — re-run at `c1f47c6` for the README paragraph.
- `check:readme-exports` and `check:doc-snippets` — **NOT MEASURED**, not green and not red. Both answered a missing prerequisite: `check:doc-snippets` printed "PRECONDITION NOT MET (exit 2) — The snippet program was NOT run" and `check:readme-exports` printed "the population COLLAPSED -- this run proves nothing" (12 packages read against a floor of 25). Both need a scoped 34-package build this round did not spend the shared box on. The README paragraph adds **no fenced block and no exported symbol**, so neither gate's population moves; CI runs them against a built tree.
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` — NOT GOVERNED, 8 paths against 5 governed surfaces, none matched.

## Acceptance notes

- **Filed, not fixed here:** objectui#9452 — a `progress`-named percent column reads a stored fraction as percentage POINTS, so the chip and the cell disagree on the magnitude. Measured in the same run as the table above; lives in `packages/fields`.
- **Filed, not fixed here:** objectui#9453 — the same chip's currency and date branches hand `Intl` a literal `undefined`, which `useDisplayLocale` documents as the one thing a caller must not do. Measured: under a `de-DE` session the chip says `Mar 4, 2026` where the cell says `4. März`. In this card's file surface but a different field family, and the precision question it raises has no contract sentence to answer it the way percent had.
- **Noted, not filed:** `summaryChipPercentPoints`'s `toPrecision(12)` was justified because "it is the TEXT that reads the result". This card took the text away, so only the invisible half of that argument survives — the chip's bar draws `7%` where the cell's draws `7.000000000000001%`, a difference no reader can see. It is kept rather than deleted, because deleting it is a rendering change of its own, and the code comment now says so. Whoever next measures the bars will carry it.
- **Duplicate check:** ⚠️ channel switch declared. The repo-scoped REST search endpoint answered `403` in this container while the repo-scoped issue READ endpoint answered `200` in the same session, so two directed MCP `search_issues` calls were used instead of a REST list plus local grep. Each carried its own lit control in its own result set (objectui#9167 / objectui#9071 / objectui#8728 for the first, objectui#4541 / objectui#4553 / objectui#4566 for the second). ⛔ No wide scan.
